Reading

Part 1 — The Basic Rules of Football

Football is a game between two teams.

Each team has eleven players.

One of those players is the goalkeeper.

The goalkeeper can use their hands inside their own goal area.

The other players can only use their feet, legs, and head — not their hands.

The goal of the game is simple: kick the ball into the other team's net.

Each time the ball goes into the net, that team scores one goal.

At the end of the game, the team with the most goals wins.

Reading

Part 2 — How Long Is a Football Match?

A standard football match has two halves.

Each half is 45 minutes long.

So a full match is 90 minutes in total.

At the end of 90 minutes, if the score is equal — for example, 1–1 — the match is a draw.

In some games, like a knockout match, a draw is not allowed.

Then the teams play extra time: two more periods of 15 minutes each.

If the score is still equal after extra time, the game is decided by a penalty shootout.

In a penalty shootout, players take turns shooting at the goal from close range.

Reading

Part 3 — What Is the 2026 World Cup?

The FIFA World Cup is the biggest football tournament in the world.

It happens every four years.

In 2026, the World Cup will be held in three countries: the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

This will be the first time three countries host the World Cup together.

The tournament will start on 11 June 2026.

There will be 104 matches in total — more than any World Cup before.

The final will be played on 19 July 2026.

Reading

Part 4 — How Teams Compete in 2026

In 2026, 48 national teams will play in the World Cup — 16 more than in the last World Cup.

The teams are divided into 12 groups.

Each group has four teams.

Inside a group, every team plays the other three teams once.

The top two teams from each group move on to the next round.

This next round is called the knockout stage, where one loss means a team is out of the tournament.

The last two teams play in the final.
